# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.

Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.

input.title: Weekly tasks: two wake on repos with nothing to work, and the fleet signal ignores dormancy
input.body:
An audit of every `frequency: 'weekly'` task's precondition, against two questions: does it wake on a declared-dormant repo, and does it wake on a repo where nothing it works has moved.

## The nine weekly tasks

Movement-gated already, nothing to do: `basics/ci-performance`, `tidy-repo/tidy-prs`, `tidy-repo/improve-comments`, `claudinite-growth/growth-dedup`.

Deliberately calendar-triggered and correct that way: `product-wiki/wiki-growth` (research arrives on the world's clock), `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-add-missing-packs` (`agent_model: 'none'` — a cheap code sweep, and every input is another repo's tree).

The three below are the findings.

## 1. The `fleet` signal has no notion of dormancy

`readFleet` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/signals/fleet.mjs` skips forks, archived repos and the canon, but never reads `dormant` from the member's declaration. So a member that declared itself out of the recurring work is still enumerated, still probed for local packs, still window-scanned commit by commit — and still lands in the member list `growth-discover-packs` (weekly, opus) and `growth-promote` (daily, opus) sweep.

Every other fleet reader gets this right (`fleet-roster`, `fleet-pack-seeds`, `fleet-add-missing-packs`, `force-fleet-baseline` all call `isDormant`); the signal layer is the one that does not. Dormancy's own contract states it: whatever looks at the repo from the outside reads the same declaration and leaves it alone.

## 2 & 3. `prose-to-checks-sweep` and `rule-revalidation` run unconditionally on a repo with no local packs

Both are weekly, opus, `precondition_signals: []`, `return { run: true }` with no arm at all. On the canon that is right — `pack_paths` is configured to include `packs/`, so there is always a corpus. On a consumer that never configures `pack_paths`, the scope defaults to `.claudinite/local/packs`, and a member that has captured nothing yet has **no such directory**: two opus sessions a week, each reading an empty scope and closing.

`growth-dedup` already gates exactly this case on `localPacks.present === false`. Its two siblings declare no signals and cannot.

## Fix

- Read `dormant` in the fleet signal's declaration reader and skip dormant members in `readFleet`, beside the fork/archived/canon skips.
- Give both growth tasks the `localPacks` signal and one gate: when `pack_paths` is unconfigured (so the scope is this repo's own local packs) and `localPacks.present` is definitively `false`, decline.

## Not changing: the weekly cadence itself

Considered and rejected — see the PR discussion. Every weekly task with a repo-side scope is already a movement-gated full sweep, which is what "do today's" would buy, and `tasks-dispatch` DESIGN §3 plus #582 are standing decisions against gate-tricking a daily task into a weekly one.

input.head: claude/weekly-tasks-preconditions-46zc7f
input.title: Weekly-task preconditions: dormant members and repos with no local packs
input.body:
Closes #1562

An audit of all nine `frequency: 'weekly'` tasks, against two questions: does the precondition wake on a declared-dormant repo, and does it wake on a repo where nothing it works has moved.

## The audit

| Task | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `basics/ci-performance` | gated on `commits`+`prs` — fine |
| `tidy-repo/tidy-prs` | gated on a PR moving in the window — fine |
| `tidy-repo/improve-comments` | gated on a substantive commit + a pending-PR arm — fine |
| `claudinite-growth/growth-dedup` | gated on `localPacks.present` + canon/local movement — fine |
| `product-wiki/wiki-growth` | calendar-triggered by design (research arrives on the world's clock), with a pending-wiki-PR arm — left alone |
| `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-add-missing-packs` | unconditional, but `agent_model: 'none'` — a cheap code sweep, and every input is another repo's tree — left alone |
| `claudinite-canon-curation/growth-discover-packs` | gated on the fleet member list, **which included dormant members** — fixed |
| `claudinite-growth/prose-to-checks-sweep` | **unconditional on a repo with no corpus** — fixed |
| `claudinite-growth/rule-revalidation` | **unconditional on a repo with no corpus** — fixed |

## 1. The fleet signal now reads dormancy

`readFleet` skipped forks, archived repos and the canon but never read `dormant`. A member that declared itself out of the recurring work was still enumerated, still probed for local packs, still window-scanned commit by commit, and still landed in the member list `growth-discover-packs` (weekly, opus) and `growth-promote` (daily, opus) sweep. Every other fleet reader already calls `isDormant` — the signal layer was the one that did not.

The skip sits beside the fork/archived ones rather than in each consuming precondition, so a dormant member costs neither an opus sweep nor the per-member probes.

## 2. The two weekly local-pack sweeps decline when there is no corpus

`prose-to-checks-sweep` and `rule-revalidation` were weekly, opus, `precondition_signals: []`, `return { run: true }`. On the canon that is right — `pack_paths` is configured to include `packs/`. On a consumer that never configures it the scope defaults to `.claudinite/local/packs`, and a member that has captured nothing has no such directory: two opus sessions a week, each reading an empty scope and closing.

Both now declare `localPacks` and decline when `pack_paths` is unconfigured **and** `present` is definitively `false` — the same test `growth-dedup` already makes. `present: null` (undetermined) still runs, and a repo that named its own `pack_paths` is never second-guessed by the local-pack probe.

The collector answers `changedInWindow` from disk in that case and left the shared commit prefetch, so the three preconditions that decline on `present === false` no longer pay a commit listing plus a detail read per window commit to say so.

## Not changed: the weekly cadence itself

Splitting the weekly "do-all" sweeps into daily "do-today's" ones was considered and not done. Every weekly task with a repo-side scope is *already* a movement-gated full sweep — which is what "do today's" would buy — and full scope is load-bearing where it exists (`tidy-prs`: a PR verdict is relative to the others, so the mover cannot be judged alone). Against it: `tasks-dispatch` DESIGN §3 (weekly is a frequency declaration, never a gate trick inside a daily task), #582 (`growth-dedup` moved daily → weekly for exactly this reason), and the canon's own standing rule that a precondition firing nearly every night buys noise, not freshness, and spends an opus session each time. Daily would take these four from ~4 opus sessions a week to ~28.

## Verification

- Both fixes written test-first and watched fail: the dormant member was enumerated (`not ok 2`), and both new gate tests returned `run: true` (`not ok 3`, `not ok 7`).
- Reachability pinned end to end in `signal-context.test.mjs` — real checkout → real ctx → these preconditions — so the gate cannot be green against a shape the collector never emits.
- Full suite: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → 2917 tests, 0 failures (the `engine-pack-lane-shims` shallow-clone guard needed `git fetch --unshallow` to run for real; it passes with history, which is what covers this change's new `isDormant` import from `engine/`).
- `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

Audited all nine weekly tasks. Six were already correct; three were not.

**Findings**

- **`fleet` signal had no notion of dormancy.** `readFleet` skips forks, archived repos and the canon — but never read `dormant`. A member that declared itself out of the recurring work was still enumerated, still probed, still window-scanned, and still swept by `growth-discover-packs` (weekly, opus) and `growth-promote` (daily, opus). Every other fleet reader calls `isDormant`; the signal layer was the one that didn't.
- **`prose-to-checks-sweep` and `rule-revalidation` ran unconditionally on a repo with no corpus.** Both weekly, opus, no signals, `run: true`. Right on the canon (`pack_paths` includes `packs/`), wrong on a consumer that never configured it: the scope defaults to `.claudinite/local/packs`, and a member that has captured nothing has no such directory — two opus sessions a week reading nothing. `growth-dedup` already gates this case; its siblings couldn't.
- Left alone deliberately: `wiki-growth` (research is on the world's clock) and `fleet-add-missing-packs` (`agent_model: 'none'`, a cheap code sweep).

Note that repo-level dormancy was never the exposure for a task's *own* repo — `scheduler-run.mjs` bails before any precondition runs. The only leak was cross-repo, through the fleet signal.

**On the weekly → daily idea: I'd keep weekly, and didn't change it.** Every weekly task with a repo-side scope is already a movement-gated full sweep — that *is* "do today's", with full scope where full scope is load-bearing (`tidy-prs`: a verdict is relative to the other open PRs). Against the flip: `tasks-dispatch` DESIGN §3, #582 (`growth-dedup` went daily → weekly for exactly this reason), and the standing rule that a nightly-firing precondition buys noise, not freshness. Daily would take these four from ~4 opus sessions/week to ~28. Say the word and I'll flip it.

## Landing it

One PR, ceilinged at `open-pr` — a change to how this repo builds or tests is always reviewed.
Reference the tracker issue in the PR body, and comment the PR link on the tracker so the week the
regression was open is legible afterwards.

If the honest answer is that the regression is real and not worth fixing — the suite grew because
the repo grew — write that on the tracker with the numbers behind it and open no PR. A measurement
that concludes "this is the correct cost" is the point of taking the measurement.

## What you must not do

- **Open the PR — that is the deliverable.** What happens to it after that is the delivery machinery's, not this run's.
- **Never make a test weaker to make it faster** — deleting coverage, dropping a case, loosening an
  assertion, or excluding a suite from the run. If a test genuinely costs more than it is worth,
  that is an argument to put to the owner on the tracker, not a change to land here.

content.text:
Reviewed all nine weekly tasks across their whole declaration — cadence, precondition, model, outcome ceiling, merge policy, timeouts, reach.

```
Task                        model   outcome  automerge policy
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
basics/ci-performance       sonnet  pr       'anything'
product-wiki/wiki-growth    opus    pr       under:product-wiki/ && doc-changes
tidy-repo/tidy-prs          sonnet  none     —
tidy-repo/improve-comments  opus    pr       comment-only-changes, readme-changes
canon/growth-discover-packs opus    pr       'nothing'
growth/rule-revalidation    opus    pr       claudinite-local-pack-md-changes
growth/prose-to-checks      opus    pr       under:<local> && markdown-line-removals,
                                             claudinite-local-pack-check-changes
growth/growth-dedup         opus    pr       under:<local> && markdown-trims
sheepdog/fleet-add-packs    none    none     —
```

**Six are coherent.** `growth-dedup` (trims only — may shrink a rule, never grow one), `prose-to-checks`' prose arm (line removals only), `wiki-growth` (`&&` intersection: a doc, *and* only under the wiki tree — a deleted doc parks, correctly), `improve-comments` (policy matches its `improve-comments-scope` check exactly, and its task.md:47 openly states the scope check is what makes it safe unattended), `growth-discover-packs` (`'nothing'` — a new canon pack every repo reads), `tidy-prs` (assess-only). On the canon, `rule-revalidation` and `prose-to-checks` both park by construction, since `packs/` is outside their policies — intended.

**Three findings, all tracing to #1464 — the commit that split `expected_outcome: 'open-pr'` into `pr` + `automerge`. It set the policies and didn't sweep the prose that stated the old ceiling.**

**1. `rule-revalidation` — its worker doc and its policy say opposite things.** `task.md:9`: *"Open a PR and leave it for review… every run's changes go in front of the owner."* `task.mjs:26`: `automerge: ['claudinite-local-pack-md-changes']` — added/modified `.md` under local packs, `editShape: any`. On a consumer, local-pack markdown *is* the entire product of a run, so on any `auto-merge` member nothing goes in front of the owner. This is also the only weekly policy that may **grow** prose unreviewed (its siblings are removals/trims), and the failure it enables is the one its own tests name as the worst outcome available to the task: a session with narrow reach rewriting a rule into "you cannot do X" — unfalsifiable afterwards, and now self-landing.

**2. `ci-performance` — two stale statements contradict the field, and the field's stated premise has two holes.** `task.mjs:19` and `task.md:33` both still say *"ceilinged at `open-pr`… always reviewed"* (retired vocabulary), while `task.mjs:33` is `automerge: 'anything'` with your 2026-08-30 note *"CI itself is the gate."* Your decision stands — the defect is the two places still asserting the old one. But the premise doesn't hold everywhere:
- `land-pr.mjs:276` — `if (!hasPrCi) return 'merge'`. On a member whose workflows are push-triggered only (Actions history exists, so the task fires), the PR merges directly with **no checks run at all**. `basics` is the baseline pack, so this ships fleet-wide.
- `merge-policy.mjs:448` returns mergeable before the loop, so bare `'anything'` is exempt from the self-widening guard at line 429 — it may land an edit to `merge-policy.mjs`, any `merge-rules.json`, any `tasks/*/task.mjs` and the policy gate itself. A sonnet weekly task holds the same authorization as the vendored-mount converge. Worth noting the cheap fix: a *list* re-engages the guard, so `['anything', 'reject:<x>']` keeps your decision and closes the policy-source hole — a single-element `['anything']` does not, it collapses back to the exempt lane.

**3. `prose-to-checks-sweep` — a stale comment, over a substantive question.** `test/tasks.test.mjs:36` asserts the outcome with *"a check can break CI → its policy is review-only"*, but the policy lists `claudinite-local-pack-check-changes`: new `declared-checks.json`, `workRules/*.mjs` and their fixtures auto-merge. That is the one weekly policy that can turn a member's own Stop hook red without a reader. Defensible (the rule ships with its see-it-fail fixture and CI runs it) — but the comment says the opposite of the declaration, so one of the two is wrong.

Structural, no action: `fleet-add-missing-packs` is the only weekly task with cross-repo write authority, and the automerge vocabulary says nothing about it — its blast radius is governed by the `--repos=all-covered-members` parameter in the declaration and the member-side task's own guards. And every policy is a *ceiling*: on a `review` member `land-pr` returns `'none'` before reading it at all.

> ⚠️ Still open: three findings above, none fixed — #2 and #3 need your call on which side is right, #1 looks like a straight sweep miss. Say which you want and I'll land them; PR [#1563](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1563) is still awaiting review.

238-
239-Task execution is **two similar, consecutive phases**: deterministic **code-work**
240-(a subprocess the executor runs, Action-side) and **agentic work** (the session
241-the executor hands off to, following task.md). Neither phase is "preparation" for the

243:runs**. That decision is the precondition's alone:
244-
245:- **The precondition sees the occurrence, not just the repo.** Its third argument is
246-  this item's own facts, for a verdict about one target where the signals describe a
247:  window of activity — a fan-out item's precondition can tell which target it is
248-  about. Declare the argument only if you read it.

251-  would not answer is a guess. The item parks open in the failure lane and the
252-  ordinary re-queue lever retries it.
253:- A task that passes its precondition **runs**. The later phases must not find
254-  "new reasons to skip" — not timing, not repo state, not "already handled", not
255-  an open PR elsewhere. If a condition should stop the run, it belongs in the

content.text:
You're right — I reviewed the wrong `policy`. Here is the precondition contract, and the nine weekly tasks against it.

**The policy** (`writing-tasks` SKILL.md §"The precondition is the ONLY decision point", plus two canon rules): the precondition is the sole run/no-run decision; **a precondition that cannot answer returns `{ error: '…' }`, never a decline** — "a decline is a decision about the world, and one taken on an API that would not answer is a guess"; its `context` lines are binding scope the agent may not re-litigate; and it gates on the objects' movement in the window, never standing state.

**Finding 1 — the error rule is enforced for the task at one evaluation point and left to the task at the other, where no weekly task implements it.**

Preconditions run **twice** per occurrence. At the anchor, `scheduler-run.mjs:668` screens every declared signal itself — `if (signals?.[n]?.error) return { error: … }` — so a failed read never reaches the precondition and fails open. At pick, `executor.mjs:353` hands `collectSignalsFor`'s output straight through (`signals.mjs:49` returns `collectSignals(...)` raw, no screen), so an errored collector arrives as `{ commits: { error: '…' } }` and every weekly precondition reads it through `?? 0` / `?? []`:

- **Declines wrongly** — `ci-performance` (`commits?.count ?? 0` → 0 → "no commits and no PR activity this week"), `tidy-prs` (→ "no open PRs"), `improve-comments`, `growth-dedup` (→ "no relevant canon or local movement").
- **Guard silently disarms** — `wiki-growth` and `improve-comments` both read `prs?.open ?? []` for their don't-stack arms. An errored `prs` signal reads as "no pending PR", so the round runs and stacks on the open one. `wiki-growth` is the sharp case: it reasons carefully about unknown-ness one level down (`opaquePr` — a PR whose `changedPaths` couldn't be read declines, because "a skipped round is cheaper than an unreviewed one") and then misses it at the signal level, where the same failure produces the outcome that arm exists to prevent.
- **Sees the error and declines anyway** — `growth-discover-packs`: `if (fleet.error) return { run: false, reason: '… (sweeping nothing on unproven fleet state)' }`. The instinct is fail-safe, but it is precisely the shape the rule names. `{ error }` parks and the re-queue lever retries; a decline burns the week.

Six of the seven signal-reading weekly tasks. The harm is concrete: the item was filed at the anchor when signals *were* readable, so at pick it closes `rejected`/not-planned, recorded as a **`success`**, with a comment asserting something false about the world. The two gates I added in [#1563](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1563) fail open on an errored signal rather than declining — correct by this rule, and the only weekly preconditions that are.

**Finding 2 — the contract document contradicts itself about where a precondition is evaluated, which is plausibly why nobody wrote the pick-side arm.** `writing-tasks/SKILL.md:28` says the scheduler run "evaluates no precondition and collects no signal" (written in #975); `:380` says "the scheduler run asks the precondition when the anchor comes, files an item only on a yes" (true since #1115). The code agrees with the second. `executor.mjs:484` still calls itself "THE only place a precondition is ever called" — also false. An author reading the contract cannot tell that there are two evaluation points, let alone that they handle a failed read differently.

**Smaller, same lane:**
- `growth-dedup`'s two run-arms are asymmetric: the canon-moved arm carries binding context ("Re-check local items against these newly-changed canon packs"), the local-changed arm carries none, so a run woken by local movement gets no pre-decided scope.
- `ci-performance` is the only agentic weekly task whose precondition pre-decides no scope at all — its scope arrives from the code-work phase's comment instead. Defensible, but it means the contract's "the precondition pre-decides scope" holds for eight of nine.
- `growth-dedup` declares `commits` and never reads it; its worker does its own commit reads. Costs nothing (`sharedMount` already triggers the shared prefetch) but it's an unread declaration.

**What's sound:** every task's verdict is pure code over signals with no later-phase skip — `task-phase-discipline` fires on none of the nine. Unknown-vs-absent is respected where it was thought about (`growth-dedup`'s `present === false`, `wiki-growth`'s `opaquePr`). Movement gating is right everywhere after #1563. And the double evaluation is safe against flips: a verdict that turns no between anchor and pick just closes the item `rejected`, which is a legal path, not a fault.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

All 25 tasks, grouped by what their precondition actually is.

```
freq     model  task                      gate                                          on an unreadable signal
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
MOVEMENT-GATED — a quiet window declines
weekly   sonnet ci-performance            commits + PR activity in the window           declines "quiet week"
weekly   opus   improve-comments          substantive commit; + no pending own PR       declines / guard off
weekly   opus   growth-dedup              mount packs moved OR local packs moved        declines
weekly   sonnet tidy-prs                  a PR opened/updated in the window             declines "no open PRs"
daily    sonnet tidy-issues               an issue touched (substantive widens scope)   declines
daily    opus   growth-extract            a substantive default-branch commit           declines
daily    opus   growth-promote            a member's local packs moved                  declines on fleet.error
daily    none   usage-fold                a commit OR a fresh conversation log          declines
daily    none   store-release             manifest ahead OR substantive change          declines (deliberate)

STATE-GATED — a standing fact, re-read each run
weekly   opus   wiki-growth               no pending wiki-tree PR                       RUNS — guard off
weekly   opus   rule-revalidation         a corpus exists to re-probe        (#1563)    runs (fails open) ✓
weekly   opus   prose-to-checks-sweep     a corpus exists to sweep           (#1563)    runs (fails open) ✓
weekly   opus   growth-discover-packs     covered members exist                         declines on fleet.error
daily    none   logs-prune                a log older than retention                    declines (deliberate)
daily    sonnet update                    a vendored mount is present                   declines

UNCONDITIONAL — no arm at all
weekly   none   fleet-add-missing-packs   —                                             n/a (no signals)
daily    none   task-janitor              —                                             n/a
daily    none   fleet-roster              —                                             n/a
daily    none   fleet-pack-seeds          —                                             n/a
monthly  sonnet jwt-advisory-watch        —                                             n/a

THE LEVER — the item's existence is the request
manual   none   verify-production / fleet-baseline / deploy-oauth-exchange
manual   sonnet adopt-requested-packs

PER-OCCURRENCE — judges the item's own target, not a window
manual   opus   implement-request         the named issue's state + eligibility         returns { error } ✓
```

**Three things the shape shows.**

**The `{ error }` rule is used by one task in twenty-five.** The contract says a precondition that cannot answer returns `{ error: '…' }` — it parks and the re-queue lever retries. `implement-request` does it (twice: an unreadable request, a missing `Request:` field). Nothing else does. Eleven tasks turn an unanswerable read into a verdict about the world instead, and the engine only catches this at one of the two evaluation points: the anchor screens signals for `.error` itself (`scheduler-run.mjs:668`), the executor at pick does not (`executor.mjs:353`), so at pick the false verdict stands and the occurrence closes `rejected` recorded as a `success`. Two tasks — `growth-promote` and `growth-discover-packs` — see `fleet.error` explicitly and decline on it in matching words. That is a convention someone chose, contradicting the written contract, so it is a decision to settle rather than a bug to patch.

**Unknown-handling has no house direction.** Four tasks reasoned about it and landed in opposite places, each defensibly: `store-release` and `logs-prune` fail closed on a null (a release is not fired on an unread checkout), `growth-dedup` and the two #1563 gates fail open (only a definite `false` may cancel a run). The other seven never considered it and inherit whichever direction `?? 0` / `?? []` happens to give. `wiki-growth` is where that bites: it reasons carefully about unknown-ness one level down — a PR whose changed paths can't be read declines, because "a skipped round is cheaper than an unreviewed one" — and an errored `prs` signal reads as "no pending PR", so the round runs and stacks, which is the outcome that arm exists to prevent.

**The unconditional block is cheap by construction, and that is load-bearing.** Four of the five run no agent at all (`agent_model: none` — code-work sweeps that no-op on a converged fleet), and `jwt-advisory-watch` is monthly. Nothing expensive is unconditional except `wiki-growth`, which is the one deliberate exception (research arrives on the world's clock). So the policy that actually governs cost is: *if it wakes a model, it has an arm* — and that now holds across all 25.

**Binding scope is near-universal but not uniform.** Twelve tasks pre-decide scope in `context`; `growth-dedup` carries it on its canon-moved arm and not its local-moved one, and `ci-performance` carries none (its scope arrives from the code-work comment instead). `implement-request` deliberately carries none, documented, because adoption already bound the item to its issue.

> ⚠️ Still open, and each is yours before we move: (1) does an unanswerable signal park (`{ error }`, per contract) or decline (per `growth-promote`/`growth-discover-packs` practice) — I'd mirror the anchor's screen at `executor.mjs:353` so no task has to remember; (2) a house direction for unknown-vs-absent, or leave it per-task; (3) `writing-tasks/SKILL.md:28` still says the scheduler evaluates no precondition, which `:380` and the code contradict. Nothing is changed yet beyond [#1563](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1563), still awaiting review.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.

Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.

Worse for my case: the seeded `RULES.md` ships with `<!-- Nothing yet. The growth lifecycle writes here; so may you. -->` — so a member that has captured nothing has `present: true` and an **empty corpus**, which is precisely the case I said the gate would catch. It tests the directory, not the content. `rule-revalidation` in [#1563](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1563) carries the identical flaw.

**Four packs run at both cadences. Three of them run the same job twice.**

- **`claudinite-growth` — `growth-extract` (daily) already does `prose-to-checks-sweep`'s (weekly) job on fresh material.** The daily capture run's last step runs the prose-to-checks skill over its own additions, so a convertible rule is converted the night it is learned. The weekly task's own cadence note says this: what is left to it is "the standing backlog — prose that has already survived at least one upgrade pass." So the weekly run's entire value is re-reading prose the daily run already declined to convert. That is the same question you are raising about its precondition, one level up.

- **`claudinite-canon-curation` — `growth-promote` (daily) and `growth-discover-packs` (weekly) both declare `precondition_signals: ['fleet']`.** That signal is a full enumeration of every owned repo, plus a local-pack probe per member, plus a per-commit window scan for each member that has them. On the weekly anchor day it runs twice, for two preconditions that then filter the same member list differently.

- **`claudinite-fleet-sheepdog` — three independent walks of the same fleet**, two daily and one weekly, all `agent_model: none`. `fleet-roster` reads coverage and freshness, `fleet-pack-seeds` reads declarations and adds seeds, `fleet-add-missing-packs` fingerprints each member's shape. Different reads, same enumeration, three separate passes over the same repo list.

- **`tidy-repo` is the one that is genuinely three jobs** — issues daily, PRs weekly, comments weekly — deliberately split so each carries its own trigger, scope and tracker with no ordering barrier between them. Not duplication.

The other five packs run at one cadence each, or one cadence plus a manual lever.

> ⚠️ Still open: your correction stands — the `localPacks.present` gate in [#1563](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1563) tests directory presence when the thing that is empty is the corpus, so it fires for a repo that deleted its pack and never for the case I justified it with. Both halves of that PR (`prose-to-checks-sweep`, `rule-revalidation`) need the same call from you: gate on corpus *content*, drop the gate and keep the calendar trigger, or reconsider whether `prose-to-checks-sweep` earns a weekly run at all given `growth-extract` already sweeps each night's new prose. Nothing changed this turn.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

input.title: Weekly-task preconditions: dormant members, and the local-pack question nobody needed to ask
input.body:
Closes #1562

An audit of all nine `frequency: 'weekly'` tasks, against two questions: does the precondition wake on a declared-dormant repo, and does it wake on a repo where nothing it works has moved. Six were already correct (`ci-performance`, `tidy-prs`, `improve-comments`, `growth-dedup` are movement-gated; `wiki-growth` is calendar-triggered by design; `fleet-add-missing-packs` runs no agent). Two findings, and a third that came out of review.

## 1. The fleet signal now reads dormancy

`readFleet` skipped forks, archived repos and the canon but never read `dormant`. A member that declared itself out of the recurring work was still enumerated, still probed, still window-scanned, and still landed in the member list `growth-discover-packs` (weekly, opus) and `growth-promote` (daily, opus) sweep. Every other fleet reader already calls `isDormant` — the signal layer was the one that did not. The skip sits beside the fork/archived ones rather than in each consuming precondition, so a dormant member costs neither an opus sweep nor the per-member probes.

## 2. Nothing asks whether a repo has local packs any more

The first pass here gated `prose-to-checks-sweep` and `rule-revalidation` on `localPacks.present === false`, reasoning that a member which has captured nothing has no `.claudinite/local/packs`. That reasoning was wrong, and the owner caught it: `seedRepoLocalPack` (`engine/converge-wiring.mjs:262`) creates the directory with a `pack.mjs` and a `RULES.md` at adoption, and the nightly deliberately never re-seeds or removes it — *"a repo that deleted its local pack made a real choice."* The seeded `RULES.md` ships carrying `<!-- Nothing yet. The growth lifecycle writes here; so may you. -->`, so a member that has captured nothing reads as **present with an empty corpus**: the gate tested the directory when the thing that is empty is the content.

So the presence question is answered by assumption everywhere, and every probe asking it was pure cost:

- `signals/fleet.mjs` drops the per-member `hasLocalPacks` contents read — one API call per member per collection, on a daily task — and computes the window scan for every declaring member.
- `signals/index.mjs` drops `present` from the `localPacks` signal; `signals/local.mjs` and `signals/context.mjs` drop the checkout probe behind it.
- `growth-dedup` gates on movement alone; `growth-promote` participates a member on its declaration.
- The two gates from the first pass are reverted — both tasks are unconditional again, as they were.

## 3. Not changed: the weekly cadence itself

Splitting the weekly "do-all" sweeps into daily "do-today's" ones was considered and not done. Every weekly task with a repo-side scope is *already* a movement-gated full sweep, and full scope is load-bearing where it exists (`tidy-prs`: a PR verdict is relative to the others, so the mover cannot be judged alone). Against it: `tasks-dispatch` DESIGN §3, #582 (`growth-dedup` moved daily → weekly for exactly this reason), and the standing rule that a precondition firing nearly every night buys noise, not freshness.

## Verification

- Each change written test-first and watched fail: the dormant member was enumerated; the fleet fixture's presence route now throws if anything probes it; the rewritten reachability test goes red when `changedInWindow` is stubbed.
- Reachability pinned end to end in `signal-context.test.mjs` — real checkout → real ctx → the precondition — under both local roots.
- Full suite: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` → 2913 tests, 0 failures. `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

Gating them on corpus *content* would be a different signal (does the local pack hold any rules yet), and you haven't asked for one — the open question from your last message, whether `prose-to-checks-sweep` earns a weekly run at all when `growth-extract` already sweeps each night's new prose, is still yours.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

contents read, the `localPacks` collector's `present`, and the checkout probe
behind it. growth-dedup now gates on movement alone, and growth-promote
participates a member on its declaration.

the seeded RULES.md ships saying "Nothing yet", so a member that has captured
nothing reads as present with an empty corpus.
